**Monday, February 29, 1960**

Your birthday has a property no other date shares: it keeps a different schedule than the rest of the calendar. While other birthdays return reliably each year, yours requires a year divisible by four — and even then, skips century years not divisible by four hundred. You have turned 66 years old. You have had sixteen actual February 29 birthdays since your first one.

What happened on those sixteen returns is worth examining, because the date has kept unusual company across history.

---

**The February 29s before you**

On February 29, 1692 — two hundred and sixty-eight years before your birth — the first warrants were issued in the Salem witch trials. Tituba, Sarah Good, and Sarah Osborne were named, and the machinery of accusation that would consume nineteen lives before it stopped was set in motion on a leap day. Salem happened, and then leap years kept happening, and eventually one of them produced you.

On February 29, 1940, the twelfth Academy Awards were held in Los Angeles. Hattie McDaniel won Best Supporting Actress for *Gone with the Wind* — the first Black person to win an Academy Award. The venue's segregation policies meant she was seated at a separate table at the back of the room, away from the rest of the film's cast and crew. She accepted the award with a composed and gracious speech. Exactly twenty years later, you were born. Twenty years after that, the Civil Rights Act had transformed American law. Twenty years after that, a Black man was elected president. The distance between Hattie McDaniel's segregated table and 2008 is sixty-eight years, most of them your lifetime.

---

**The day itself**

On February 29, 1960 — your birth day — an earthquake struck the Moroccan city of Agadir just after midnight. It was relatively modest in magnitude but catastrophically shallow, rupturing directly beneath the city's densest neighborhoods. Between twelve and fifteen thousand people died in seconds, in a city of thirty thousand. Morocco had been independent for only four years. The disaster reshaped international building codes and disaster response for decades. The world that received you was already carrying that news.

---

**Twenty-eight days before you arrived**

On February 1, 1960 — four weeks before your birth — four Black college students sat down at the Woolworth's lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina and refused to leave when denied service. Within days the tactic had spread to other cities. Within weeks, dozens of sit-ins were underway across the South. The Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee was founded two months later. The civil rights movement was entering its most consequential decade, and you arrived at its inflection point.

---

**Your sixtieth birthday**

On February 29, 2020 — the day you turned sixty, one of your rare actual birthdays — the United States recorded its first confirmed COVID-19 death. A patient in Washington State, cause of death announced that afternoon. It was the beginning of what would become a years-long disruption of ordinary life that most people alive at the time will carry as a permanent before-and-after. You turned sixty on the day the American pandemic began.

---

**The year itself**

1960 is sometimes called the Year of Africa — seventeen nations gained independence from European colonial rule in a single calendar year. Cameroon, Togo, Madagascar, Senegal, Mali, Congo, Ivory Coast, Niger, Chad, Nigeria, and others: the map of a continent was redrawn before you could walk. The world you were born into was being administratively reorganized at a speed that had no modern precedent.

In May 1960, the FDA approved the birth control pill — three months after your birth. The transformation that followed in women's autonomy, family structure, and the workforce unfolded across the decades of your life. In November 1960, John F. Kennedy was elected president, the youngest ever, promising a new generation in power. You were eight months old. The decade that followed — Kennedy, then Johnson, then Nixon, Vietnam, the moon landing, the assassinations — formed the texture of your childhood.

---

**The arc**

You are 66. You were born before the Sputnik era had fully registered in American consciousness, before the first American in space, before the interstate highway system was complete, before the polio vaccine was universal. You were nine when humans walked on the Moon. Twenty-nine when the Berlin Wall fell. Forty-one on September 11, 2001. Sixty when the pandemic began on your actual birthday. Sixty-six now, in the early years of artificial intelligence as a daily presence.

Your birthday has witnessed warrants issued in a witch trial, a watershed moment in the history of American racism, a city destroyed by an earthquake, and the opening day of a global pandemic. It comes back around every four years with new cargo.

Sixty-six years. Sixteen real birthdays. A life measured in leap days and everything that happened between them.
